terminologyRules: Feline asthma is chronic inflammatory lower-airway disease with hyperreactivity and reversible bronchoconstriction, not a synonym for any cough or bronchial image.
There is no single accepted clinical gold-standard test; diagnosis integrates compatible disease and explicit exclusions.
Asthma, chronic bronchitis, lungworm, heartworm-associated respiratory disease, pneumonia, edema, neoplasia, pleural disease and foreign body remain distinct states.
Blood or airway eosinophilia is not specific for asthma and never bypasses regional parasite and heartworm assessment.
Breed, one symptom, one image or response to an unreviewed trial never confirms asthma alone.
Minimal handling and oxygen precede radiography, BAL or bronchoscopy in unstable cats.
A quiet chest in an exhausted cat can represent critically poor airflow rather than improvement.
Rescue-only use is not complete chronic inflammatory control.
Device prescription is incomplete until mask/spacer technique and owner-cat feasibility are observed.
Episode history, oxygenation, imaging, sample truth, environment and response are authored before player choice and persist through reload.
Drug, dose, taper, actuation count, oxygen target and emergency airway/procedure technique require separately approved protocols.

familyValidationRules: Reject if oxygen and minimal handling are delayed for complete diagnostics in a dyspneic cat.
Reject if a quiet chest in an exhausted cat is recorded as normal or improving.
Reject if breed, eosinophilia, one radiograph or bronchodilator response alone confirms asthma.
Reject if lungworm or heartworm content appears without compatible region and exposure.
Reject if neutrophils alone generate an antimicrobial indication or all lower-airway disease is collapsed into asthma.
Reject if the generator creates a drug, dose, emergency procedure, device prescription or ventilation setting.
